qs.q: The angle between the true great-circle track and the true rhumb-line track joining A (60°S 165°W) and B (60°S 177°E), at the place of departure A, is:
qs.ex: d.long = 15° + 3° = 18°. Convergency = 18 × sin 60° ≈ 15.6°; conversion angle = ½ ≈ 7.8°.

qs.q: The average true course of the great circle is 100°. The true course of the rhumb line at point A is:
qs.ex: The rhumb line track equals the great circle track at the mid-point (the average).

qs.q: What is the standard formula for convergency?
An aircraft passes position A (60°00′N 120°00′W) en route to position B (60°00′N 140°30′W). What is the great circle track on departure from A?
qs.ex: RL is 270°. Convergency = 20.5 × sin 60° ≈ 17.8°, CA ≈ 8.9°. In the NH the GC lies on the polar side, so the initial GC track is 270 + 9 ≈ 279°.

qs.q: A great circle track joins position A (59°S 141°W) and B (61°S 148°W). What is the difference between the great circle track at A and B?
qs.ex: Convergency = 7 × sin 60° ≈ 6°. Going west in the SH the GC track increases.

qs.q: The rhumb line track between position A (45°00′N 010°00′W) and position B (48°30′N 015°00′W) is approximately:
The great circle track from P to Q measured at P is 095°, southern hemisphere, conversion angle P–Q = 7°. What is the rhumb line track P–Q?
qs.ex: In the SH the GC lies south of the RL; eastbound, the initial GC track (095) is more southerly than the RL: RL = 095 − 7 = 088°.

qs.q: The great circle track X–Y measured at X is 319° and at Y 325°. Which statement is correct?
o: southern hemisphere, rhumb line track is 331°
northern hemisphere, rhumb line track is 313°
southern hemisphere, rhumb line track is 322°
qs.ex: GC track increases from 319 to 325 (by 6°) going north-west: SH. RL = mean = 322°.

qs.q: Place A is at 70°00′S 060°00′W and place B 70°00′S 030°00′E. Find the initial great circle track.
qs.ex: d.long 90°, convergency = 90 × sin 70 ≈ 84.6°, CA ≈ 42.3°. RL = 090°; in the SH the GC starts towards the pole (south): 090 + 42 = 132°.

qs.q: On a Mercator chart the GC track from A (25°00′S 010°00′W) to B (35°00′S 040°00′W) is 242°. Find the RL track from B to A.
qs.ex: Mean lat 30°S, d.long 30°: convergency 15°, CA 7.5°. In the SH the GC lies on the southern (polar) side; westbound RL A→B = 242 + 7.5 = 249.5°, so B→A = 069.5°.
